label: alg:jet-prefix-transport
title: Jet-prefix transport in the $q \to 1$ limit
html:
Algorithm. Jet-prefix transport in the q \to 1 limit

Algorithm (Jet-prefix transport, q \to 1 limit). Truncate the Markov-trace Laurent polynomial at jet order N and transport its leading coefficients to the archimedean fibre at q = q_0 via the GS filtration of Step 7.

Input

  • Markov-trace polynomial P_K(q) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathrm{NF}(K)) (output of Step 3, evaluated symbolically).
  • Target jet order N \in \mathbb{N} (chosen by precision goal — default N = \lceil \log_{10}(1/\varepsilon) / 2.07 \rceil - 1).

Output

  • Truncated polynomial P_K^{(N)}(q) = \sum_{d = -N}^{N} c_d \, q^d with |P_K(q) - P_K^{(N)}(q)| = O(h^{N+1}) where h = q - 1.

Algorithm

1. Expand P_K(q) around q = 1 as a Taylor / Laurent series in h.
2. Retain terms up to order h^N.
3. Match length levels ℓ to jet orders d via the GS-filtration
   correspondence (`prop:jet-prefix-gb-filtration`).
4. Return the truncated polynomial with jet-order metadata.

Correctness conditions

  1. prop:jet-prefix-gb-filtration gives the length \leftrightarrow jet-order correspondence used in step 3.
  2. prop:gb-spectral-sequence (E_2 collapse, Step 7) ensures the truncation does not mix orders.

Complexity

O(N \cdot \dim H_n(q)) — linear in the target jet order and in the Hecke dimension.

Python API entry point

Canonical compute is the script computations/gb_filtration_jet_order_reader.py, which reads the GS-filtered NF and emits the per-jet-order truncation witness. The substrate's precision discipline (compute at 70 dps, serialise at 60 dps) is configured by qou_substrate.precision.

Witness contract

Canonical witness: gb-filtration-jet-order-reader.witness.json. Records the truncated polynomial, the jet-order metadata, and a cross-check against the symbolic Taylor expansion.

Notes

The jet-prefix truncation gates symbolic (q-exact) compute from archimedean evaluation at q_0. Target precision determines N. See the c_k truncation sidecar for the analogous truncation in the \mathfrak{Q}_\beta ladder.
